# Lane 2.227: the independent review, 2026-11-26

Read: the step, the lane note, T-472 to T-475, the whole diff. Run: the role matrix with `packages/core/src/modules/access`, `list-postponed-games` and `read-league-settings` (20 files, 346 passed); `reads-in-core-test` (17), `scoring-screen-test` (1002), `live-game-test` (41), `needs-result-test` (33); two throwaway probes in the lane's `.local/` (served HTML and `?_rsc` answers). Nothing of the step's code was changed.

## Findings

- **Medium.** `tests/browser/reads-in-core-test.mjs` line 139 looks for a setting key as `"key"`, but in the data sent to the client a key is spelled `\"key\"`, so a key sent but not drawn is never found. Seen: a break that hands every league setting key to a client component (`IntoView words=…`) for the refused admin; my probe found all 12 keys in the HTML and the `?_rsc` answer, and the test still passed, 17 of 17. Mend: look for the bare key (`body.includes(key)`; the keys are distinctive), and also fetch the page with `RSC: 1` (a client-side navigation) and check that answer the same way.
- **Medium.** T-474, `stand-in-cast.ts` line 52 and the lane note say Settings stays open to a program's admin "for the Admins page of their program". It does not: `admins-page.tsx` line 47 asks `list_access` for the whole league and answers 403 (probe: 403). The admin of one program is drawn an Admins row that leads to "You do not have access". Core's `list_access` and `invite` take a program scope, but no page offers it, so today a program's admin can manage their program's access nowhere. The builder is right about 2.97's page; the step's line is wrong. Mend: correct T-474's wording and the comment now; hide the Admins row when `list_access` refuses, or (a product choice for the lead, "Decided for you") let the Admins page list and invite at the holder's program scope.
- **Low.** Same test, line 211: "the schedule is not theirs to open" passes on a 500 (`status !== 200`). Served today: 403. Mend: `status === 403`.
- **Low.** T-472 says the games a scorekeeper scores "bring their own place and time". Time yes (the probe's rows: "Sun, Nov 22, 7:00 PM"); the games reads carry no place at all (no venue in the games module, no staff games list shows one). Not a loss from this step. Mend: say "time", or name where the place is read.
- **Low.** `run-publish.ts` lines 40 and 62 tell someone who may not publish `illegal-transition` before `not-allowed` (the league's state). Nothing new: the staff shell already sends every staff member `data-status="draft"`. Mend, if wanted: answer `not-allowed` first when `may` is false.
- **Low.** The role matrix has no archived-league case for `leagues.read_league_settings`: my break (`mayEditLeague` in place of `mayChangeLeagueSettings`) passed the matrix and was caught only by `read-league-settings.test.ts`. Enough, but the "any state" rule rests on one test.

1. Scorekeeper in core: held. The matrix refuses `get_schedule_draft`, `list_venues`, `list_postponed_games` and every `schedule.*` command with `not-allowed`; the `games.score` reads answer only their games (time, teams, no draft, no venues). Served: Schedule and Settings 403; the games list has no postponed part and no draft mark; scoring passes (the three tracker tests above).
2. Other holders of `schedule.read`: held. It is named only in core; no migration stores a permission (grants and invitations store a role); the rehearsal script signs in no scorekeeper; the tracker routes use `games.score`. A club admin still holds it (not this step's).
3. Admin of one program: held. HTML and `?_rsc`: 200, no setting key, no privacy sentence, no profile or publish part. Every settings action's command checks the whole league in core (`mayChangeSetting` at league scope, `mayEditLeague`, `mayChangeLeagueSettings`); read in code and the matrix, not posted over HTTP (action ids). `readNamePolicy` elsewhere is the public name rule.
4. `list_postponed_games`: held (its tests pass; the rule is `schedule.read` at each season's program, so two programs give both, league-wide gives all, and a not-public season of A is A's own scheduler's).
5. Kept names: held. The other pages that read every name use them on the server only; no redirect carries a name; a saved notice's game is named only after the box score read answered. The import count is `get_schedule_draft`'s own (stand-in only: no database implementation yet).
6. Admins page: the builder is right (Medium above).
7. Tests passing for the wrong reason: got through (Medium and Low above). Breaks: the browser break above (missed); the matrix break above (missed by the matrix, caught by the core test). Both put back; the build was made again from HEAD and `reads-in-core-test` passed.
8. T-472 to T-475: none takes from a role more than the step's line; T-474's and T-472's wording as above.
9. Rows saved before: grants and waiting invitations hold a role, so a scorekeeper's loses `schedule.read` at once, and an invitation accepted later gives `games.score` only. Access is read on every command (`accessOfAccount`), so an open session loses it at its next request.
